setting: Tomas runs a woodshop and writes every text in full sentences. Tex has his Context notes, Google Calendar, a reminder tool and the web. His calendar has a 3:00 PM call with Dr. Lee on Tuesday and a 10:00 AM client meeting on Wednesday.
title: Tomas and Tex: his full sentences

msgs.text: Good morning. Could you move my call with Dr. Lee to Thursday at the same time?

must: confirm in Tomas's register: capitals and full stops, a few words
never: read his whole request back to him

msgs.text: Done. It's on Thursday at 3:00 PM now.
Thank you. What time is my meeting on Wednesday?
I have had the longest week. Please tell me it is nearly Friday.

must: a friend's one-line reply in his register

msgs.text: It's Thursday evening, so very nearly. Hang in there.
Ha. Could you remind me at 5 tomorrow to send the contract?
What do you think of ending emails with "Best" rather than "Kind regards"?

must: a take with a reason, in his register: capitals and full stops, a line or two

msgs.text: "Best" reads warmer and quicker. I'd keep "Kind regards" for a first email to a new client.
